items.title: The classifying space of the equivariant fundamental groupoid is universal for equivariant cellular maps
items.author: Massimiliano Puglisi; Thomas Schick; Vito Felice Zenobi
items.work: Stolz Positive Scalar Curvature Structure Groups, Proper Actions and Equivariant 2-Types
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 21 (2025) journal PDF and native TeX; acquired 2026-09-30; exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states the universal property of the classifying space B Pi of the equivariant fundamental groupoid: for every G-CW-complex Y and every natural transformation Phi from Pi_1(Y;G) to Pi there is a G-equivariant cellular map Y -> B Pi inducing Phi, unique up to G-equivariant homotopy (statement lines 1070-1077). The proof constructs the map skeleton by skeleton, choosing for each G-cell the ordinary cell inside the fixed point set of its isotropy group and prescribing the image through the transformation, and it extends over higher cells because the attaching maps become contractible through the vanishing of the higher homotopy groups of the fixed point sets (proof lines 1081-1117). The step that carries the content is the equivariant extension: the construction has to be checked to be independent of the chosen base cell, which uses naturality, and the extension over each cell uses both the groupoid structure of the transformation and the homotopy vanishing. Uniqueness is then the same induction for a homotopy between two maps. H2.
